title: American Beech: Ancient American Beeches You Can Visit
meta_description: The smooth-barked beech of the eastern forests. Atlanta's Grandfather Beech stands 36.7 metres tall; Jacob Riis planted two in Queens in 1905.
intro: American beech is the beech of the eastern North American forests, its bark smooth and silver-grey for life, its dry copper leaves often hanging on through winter until spring pushes them off. Atlanta's Grandfather Beech is 36.7 metres tall and 3.45 metres round, third among the city's beeches, and Atlanta Magazine dates it to 1863, the summer before the Battle of Atlanta, without saying how it knows. In Washington, Beatrix Farrand found a two-acre beech grove already standing when she laid out Dumbarton Oaks Park around 1930, and made it the way in. In Queens, Jacob Riis planted two beside his wife's grave in 1905. At Serenbe, south-west of Atlanta, one leans out over a creek where it drops off a granite slab. And in Coeur d'Alene, far west of anywhere the species grows wild, somebody planted one in a front garden, and it now rises far above the house.
